description:
Make well-known repository file paths compile-time constants and derive repair-path test coverage from the repair planner's own declaration instead of a hand-maintained list.

## Background

`VirtualPath` is `String`-backed through `RootRelativePath::Descendant(String)` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs:13-19`), which blocks `const`. There are ~100 production `VirtualPath::data("literal")?` call sites (for example `gates.toml`, `events.jsonl`, `config.toml`, `index.json`, `rules.toml`), each a fallible construction of a compile-time-known-good value.

**Path constants.** Change the payload to `Cow<'static, str>`. `Cow::Borrowed` is const-constructible, so well-known paths become `pub const` associated items (`VirtualPath::GATES`, `EVENTS`, `CONFIG`, `INDEX`, `RULES`, ...) and the fallible `VirtualPath::data("literal")?` sites become infallible const references. Parsing and deserialization produce `Cow::Owned`; `Ord`/`Hash`/`Eq` semantics are unchanged (`Borrowed("x") == Owned("x")`), so const and parsed keys collide correctly in the `BTreeMap`-keyed image. Because consts bypass the reserved-path `checked()` guard (`path.rs:173-186`), one test iterates every associated const via a `VirtualPath::ALL_KNOWN` list, asserting round-trip equality through the fallible constructor -- proving each const canonical and non-reserved.

**Derived repair coverage.** The repair test at `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/derived_state_repair_tests.rs:85-110` re-lists 11 repair paths by hand as `repair_paths()`, paired with a loose `assert!(count >= 5)`, so a new derived target silently under-covers. Two facts shape the fix: every family in `derive_repair` (`repository_state/mod.rs:660-701`) is drift-filtered -- projections skip when bytes already match (`materialize.rs:351-357`), the default ruleset writes only on diff (`materialize.rs:432,456-459`), profile targets push only when the entry differs (`mod.rs:680-697`) -- so a set derived from walked actions would enumerate only currently-drifting paths; and the 11 literals mix repair write-targets with three fixture-input-only paths (`index.json`, `events.jsonl`, the profile record) that `derive_repair` never writes.

Add a new public introspection API `repository_state::repair_target_paths(image, declarations, profiles) -> Result<BTreeSet<VirtualPath>>` that enumerates the complete drift-independent set of paths repair may materialize: default-ruleset targets guarded by the capture spec (via `serialized_default_ruleset(config).schema_files`), configured-projection targets (via `require_target`), and the keys of `compose_profile_targets` per claims. Obsolete-schema deletions stay excluded by definition -- their targets are occupant-proven paths deliberately outside the declared set (`materialize.rs:498-512`). `derive_repair` is **not** refactored to consume it (it needs composed bytes per target, which a path set cannot supply); instead the authority relationship is enforced by a unit test asserting every non-delete action target of `derive_repair` is a member of `repair_target_paths` on the same inputs. The repair test's hand-list is replaced by `repair_paths() = repair_target_paths(...) union {index.json, events.jsonl, profile record}` (the three fixture-input paths as an explicit tail), and it gains a full-drift coverage assertion: seed every target stale and assert the repair delta's write/set-mode target set equals `repair_target_paths(...)` exactly.

`repair_target_paths` is an ordinary public API of `repository_state` -- a declarative introspection surface in the same spirit as validation -- so both the in-crate subset test and the integration coverage test call it without `test-support` gating.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `VirtualPath` is `Cow<'static, str>`-backed and the well-known repository paths are `pub const` associated items, replacing the ~100 fallible `VirtualPath::data("literal")?` construction sites with infallible const references, with `Ord`/`Hash`/`Eq` semantics preserved so const and parsed keys collide correctly.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test iterates every associated const via `VirtualPath::ALL_KNOWN` and asserts round-trip equality through the fallible constructor, proving each const canonical and non-reserved.
- [hard] REQ-03: A public `repository_state::repair_target_paths(image, declarations, profiles) -> Result<BTreeSet<VirtualPath>>` enumerates the drift-independent repair-target set (default-ruleset targets, configured-projection targets, profile-target keys; obsolete-schema deletions excluded), and a unit test asserts every non-delete `derive_repair` action target is a member of `repair_target_paths` on the same inputs.
- [hard] REQ-04: The repair test replaces its hand-maintained list with `repair_target_paths(...)` plus the three explicit fixture-input paths, and asserts under full seeded drift that the repair delta's write/set-mode target set equals `repair_target_paths(...)` exactly.

## Notes

Both the subset unit test and the full-drift coverage test call `repair_target_paths` without any `test-support` feature gating and with no dependency on the feature-gating hygiene task. The suite must not add any integration-test target.
title: Compile-time path constants and derived repair-path coverage
